note: Steps of the plan, by milestone. gather.py keeps a 'done' or 'done-emu' step only while every pull request it names is merged with CI passing on the commit that brought it into main; otherwise it drops the step to 'review' or 'progress' and says why. The tag of each step (merged, in review, in progress or planned) comes from gh. 'done-emu' means checked on the host, in WASM under Node and Bun, or in headless DOSBox; nothing has run on real hardware. Milestones 0 to 6 are the working plan, with Milestone 1.5 (id m1_5) between Milestones 1 and 2, Milestone 3.5 (id m3_5) after Milestone 3 and Milestone 6 (Shell) last; Milestones 3.5 and 6 are placeholders with no start date; the order of Milestones 2 to 5 follows the restart plan in docs/POC-1-FINDINGS.md.

milestones.label: M1 · The first playable slice
milestones.next: The documentation phase: this archive refresh and the release changelog. The rest of the milestone is merged.

milestones.label: M1.5 · Machine, settings and DOS audio
milestones.next: Remaining: the frame-rate policy (/FPS30, /FPS60 and /FPSAUTO, benched with music running), the HUD without TICK, the Options screen with the Motion setting on DOS, and the HUD extras. Done: the probes, /CHECK (#52), the sound settings (#55), /? (#67), DOS audio (#62), and the OPL3 channel pair with positional sound (#74). The milestone's own test, the cluck audible on DOS, has not been done because nobody has listened. It runs in parallel with the music of Milestone 4.

milestones.label: M2 · Content pipeline
milestones.next: The real work has not started. The sprite grids and the generated sprite data exist; the first fizz-bake step is a Level Studio script baked into a Fizz Asset Pack (`.FAP`), with a per-target profile. The Fizz 1 survey adds the enemy roster with animation states, animated tiles, backdrop art for parallax and the export of the stars sprite. New Episode 2 design, not ports: idle blinks and orbiting dizzy stars, with run dust and a landing squash proposed.

milestones.label: M3 · Scene intent and camera
milestones.next: The real work has not started. A shared pixel rule, a stateless look offset and the shared drawing exist; fizz-engine with scene intent is next, then the camera with Fizz 1's pixel-locking, shown on Web and DOS. The Fizz 1 survey adds Fizz 1's camera constants and Tower mode, shake for the remaining events, drawing between ticks on Web, point lights with a DOS 16-colour shade pass, night profiles, parallax layers and a general effects list.

milestones.label: M3.5 · Mechanics roster
milestones.next: Placeholder with no start date. Nothing is started. Wall-kick comes first, because the lighthouse level is vertical; score, snacks and lives wait for an Episode 2 decision.

milestones.label: M4 · Audio
milestones.next: Music runs in parallel with the end of Milestone 1.5. The level music is 'Crater Fields', Fizz 1's track used as a placeholder test song and not an official Fizz 2 track: its source (#73) and its Web player (#75) are merged, the lowering to OPL2 and OPL3 (package B) is in progress, and the DOS player and the music documents follow. The IMF lab songs stay as the later replacement. Fizz 1's other sound effects for the slice with their captions, the full caption table (including whoa!) and stereo-authored effects are planned.

milestones.label: M5 · CI gates and the 486 budget
milestones.next: Keeps the CI cycle gate and the size budgets. /BENCH, its calibration line and the tracked size exist; the budgets are measured against a 486DX model and gated in CI.

milestones.label: M6 · Shell
milestones.next: Placeholder with no start date. Nothing is started: title, pause, options, four save slots, result cards and the opening cinematic; haptics and a debug level select come later.

nodes.label: Death shake
nodes.what: A screen shake of at most a pixel for 18 ticks, derived from Ben's dead state, so the rules gain no new state. The Web Motion button turns it off; DOS always shakes. No still shows it, and it has not been looked at on DOS.

nodes.label: Death spin
nodes.what: Ben turns about his centre as he dies, at Fizz 1's rate, by rotating the ben_jump sprite in integers from a baked cosine and sine table indexed by the ticks since death. View only, and under the Motion setting with the shake: Reduced keeps the flat flickering pose. Pinned as frame digests; nobody has looked at it on DOS.
nodes.evidence: fizz-slice-view tests (ten death frames in both settings)

nodes.label: The OPL3 channel pair (P-F)
nodes.what: OPL3 detection, and the cluck on the pair: channel 5 for the left ear (output bit 0x10) and channel 14 in the second bank for the right (0x20), each at its own carrier level, with the OPL3 switched on and back off. It replaced the centre-only channel 14. Checked in DOSBox; not on a real OPL3.

nodes.label: Positional sound
nodes.what: The cluck sounds where its chicken is on screen, by Fizz 1's pan and distance formula, written once as a pure integer function (fizz_sfx::place). The pair takes a level for each ear; OPL2 and AdLib take the distance as a level; the speaker ignores it. The Web gives each voice a stereo panner and a gain, with a Classic or Enhanced button in the H panel (Enhanced by default). The rules never see the placement. Explained in docs/SFX.md, Placing sounds. Nobody has listened.
nodes.evidence: docs/SFX.md; cargo test -p fizz-sfx; web/sfx.test.ts; tools/check-dos.sh AUDIO WRITES per path

nodes.label: fizz-engine scene intent

nodes.label: View info, never the rules
nodes.what: The size of the viewport is reported to the view and the camera code and never to the rules: wake and activation use fixed tile distances, so the state hash is the same at every window size. A hard constraint for the engine. It landed for the Web in #60 (App::set_view); DOS has one fixed view.
